long_biography.plain_text:
Airport Equipment Rentals emerged from a setback rather than a tidy business plan. Jerry Sadler and his brother Jay had invested earnings from Alaska's pipeline era in housing, commercial property and a construction operation. When oil prices fell and the local property market contracted, their equipment and workforce suddenly exceeded the work available. Customers began asking to rent tools and machinery they were trying to sell, revealing a different way forward.

The brothers launched the rental company in 1986 from a small building on Airport Road. Sadler expanded beyond Fairbanks into a six-location network selling, renting and servicing heavy equipment for construction, mining, logging and energy projects. The family business added vehicle rental and developed successive generations of managers while preserving Alaska-based employment. Sadler remains its owner and president, with the company continuing to rank among the state's largest locally owned enterprises.
